# T(2,n), the number of positive friezes over (1/2)Z of width n.
# Proved-complete: the search box is a_i <= (n-4)N^2+2N, the Cuntz-Holm entry
# bound, VERIFIED in the library as cuntz_holm_bound.  Regenerated by
# code/width_sequence.py.
#
# n, T(2,n)
4, 4
5, 20
6, 102
7, 511
8, 2576
9, 13101
#
# Not in OEIS (checked 2026-08-16; the Catalan control returns matches, this
# returns none).  T(1,n) is the Catalan number C_{n-2}.
# No P-recursive recurrence of order 1 with degree-1 polynomial coefficients:
# the 5-by-4 system from these six terms has rank 4, so only the trivial
# solution.
#
# WHY THE SEQUENCE STOPS HERE.  A recurrence of order r with coefficients of
# degree d has (r+1)(d+1) unknowns and K-r equations from K terms, so the test
# is vacuous whenever K-r < (r+1)(d+1).  With six terms only (r,d) = (1,1) is
# testable, and it fails.  Seven terms would add (1,2) as a binary test with no
# confirmation; nine terms are needed before any order-2 class is informative.
#
# The enumeration cost tracks the raw box: measured wall times for N = 1..2 are
# 0.54 s at width 8 and 74 s at width 9, a ratio of 137 against a raw box ratio
# of 120, so the pruning gives no asymptotic help.  Extrapolating, width 10 is
# about 2.9 hours, width 11 about 20 days, width 12 about 9 years.
#
# So the ninth term is out of reach by this method and the question of whether
# T(2,n) is P-recursive is blocked by the algorithm, not by patience.  A
# transfer-matrix enumeration over path states was the natural alternative and
# was killed at its consistency pass: the frieze column entries grow by about a
# factor 2.4 per width, so that state space is exponential too.
